review_evidence: README states that Lean-for-Lean implements the Lean 4 kernel in Lean and also houses metatheory about Lean in the direction of MetaCoq.
64 of 102 Lean files contain theorem/lemma/example/axiom declarations, with 2,376 declaration hits in the snapshot.

Lean4Lean/Theory develops verified environment/level-satisfiability and kernel-related metatheory; representative declarations include VEnv order lemmas and many LevelSat evaluation bounds, so the source is not merely implementation tooling.
summary: Reviewed lean4lean; retain the Lean-kernel implementation together with its substantial Lean metatheory.

review_evidence: Ran the declaration-keyword grep across all 29 listed files: only Lean4Lean/Tests/Environment.lean matched zero; every other file matched between 1 and 251.

Read Lean4Lean/Tests/Environment.lean in full: `import Lean4Lean.Environment`, a doc comment, `namespace Lean4Lean.Tests.Environment`, `open Lean`, and a `run_meta` block that builds a partial-safety variant of Nat.add and checks Primitive.checkDef rejects it -- an executable regression test, not an import-only file.

Confirmed Lean4Lean/FuelConfig.lean (1 match) and Lean4Lean/Verify/Environment/Primitive/Gcd.lean (1 match) each carry at least one genuine declaration despite the low count, consistent with small focused files rather than stubs.

Spot-checked the largest files: Lean4Lean/Verify/Environment/Primitive/Condition.lean (190849 bytes, 107 declarations), Lean4Lean/Verify/Environment/Primitive/Recursion.lean (119079 bytes, 30 declarations), Lean4Lean/Verify/Typing/Lemmas.lean (104271 bytes, 251 declarations), Lean4Lean/Verify/Environment/Primitive/Basic.lean (81253 bytes, 147 declarations) -- consistent with a large genuine kernel-correctness proof development.
summary: Ran a declaration-keyword grep over all 29 changed/added files. Only one matched zero: Lean4Lean/Tests/Environment.lean, read in full -- it is not a pure import aggregator (it has `open Lean` and a `run_meta` executable command, which take it outside that class per FILTER-007): it is a genuine front-end kernel-hardening regression check that constructs a partial-safety copy of Nat.add and asserts Primitive.checkDef correctly rejects it, per its own doc comment ('Front-end declaration checks that are not covered by Lean4Lean.Tests.KernelHardening'). Retained as real verification content. Every other file matched between 1 (Lean4Lean/FuelConfig.lean, Lean4Lean/Verify/Environment/Primitive/Gcd.lean) and 251 (Lean4Lean/Verify/Typing/Lemmas.lean) declaration keywords, consistent with the prior review's characterization of the Lean-kernel implementation (Environment, Primitive, TypeChecker) together with its Lean metatheory (Theory/Typing, Theory/VExpr) and its correctness-verification layer (Verify/*). No file meets the FILTER-002/FILTER-004 evidence bar for exclusion; retain all 29.
